question:
(i) Explain the significance of choosing a Gaussian surface while applying Gauss’s law.
(ii) Does the total electric flux through a closed surface depend on the shape and size of the surface? Justify your answer.

options.A:
(i) A Gaussian surface is selected only to enclose the largest possible charge
(ii) Flux increases when surface area or volume increases
options.B:
(i) A Gaussian surface must always be cubic
(ii) Flux is always zero through every closed surface
options.C:
(i) A Gaussian surface is chosen to match symmetry and simplify the flux calculation
(ii) Total flux is $\Phi=\frac{q_{\text{in}}}{\varepsilon_0}$ and depends only on net enclosed charge, not shape or size
options.D:
(i) The Gaussian surface changes the electric field produced by charges
(ii) Flux depends only on the material of the surface
